### application-core reuse R1: the native property cache, a property projection of the canonical claim in the existing proof store

change `sktkmnpnoqsv` · [log `e77a9a79565f`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/e77a9a79565f6c97a8533e2a7f7f238645f3d119ad5aee7236e6154d3c10cd20.jsonl.gz)

prove --cache DIR now keeps a property check's verified and refuted results in the regression proofs' store (lib/src/reuse.rs), keyed by the same canonical claim digest. The claim projects the target's parameters, the closure of the target and of every constructor its inputs, result and declared exceptions are made with, the assumption, assertion, throws clauses, the meaning of \old, the null and alias choices, any construction plan, the bounds and the checker's settings. A first assumption marks it a property claim, so it never shares a key with a regression claim of the same target. Every field of property::Options is named in the projection; an unknown one, or an engine other than the own checker, refuses the check under --cache instead of keying without it. A verified hit gives back the stored outcome and statement, marked as reused. A refutation is stored with the harness it was found in, and reused only once its witness fails that harness again on the current classes. Nothing unresolved is stored.

Verified inline: lib/tests/reuse.rs (7 tests, on the frozen quote fixture and small builds, native engine, no JBMC): exact hits of both kinds, a stale stored witness proved again, an input's changed constructor invalidating the proof of an unchanged method (the test fails with the constructor roots taken out), a key per assertion, assumption, throws clause, domain, bound and plan history, none for an unrelated change. The contract's R1 now verifies cold and on the rerun; 230 unit tests, tests/application_core.rs and tests/summaries.rs pass, clippy is clean. Interface requests for property.rs and main.rs are under the stream brief's Progress.

The integration contract's J3 now passes on distinct keys instead of on the refusal. 230 unit tests and the contract, summaries, heap, effects and foundations suites pass.

Also recorded under Progress: an unsound regression-cache hit the objects stream found in proof_cache.rs (an inner object's constructor is missing from the closure's roots), which is this stream's next piece of work.

### application-core reuse: a regression claim's closure rooted at every constructor its harness calls, an inner object's included

change `qssovxorxqsy` · [log `76a89868444d`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/76a89868444d0ef14c44507dd64f5cdb99d29e1b5d5e25cdc61e787a4c0658f1.jsonl.gz)

proof_cache::Regression::claim rooted each version's closure at a made object's own constructor only, not at the constructors of the objects it is made from, which the harness calls too. The claim now roots both versions, and a previous version's receiver and records, at every constructor RecordType::constructors lists.

Reproducer first: tests/reuse.rs's an_inner_objects_constructor_in_either_version_is_part_of_a_regression_claim failed before the fix with an exact hit on the changed build. It now checks that a rewrite is verified and reused on an unchanged rerun, and that a change to the inner constructor after, and then before, misses the cache and is refuted. Also fixed: tests/reuse.rs compiled each build into a shared directory it removed first, so parallel tests could remove each other's classes. Each build is now compiled once per run. Verified inline: tests/reuse.rs (11 tests, three runs), the 230 unit tests, and the application_core, compare, effects, foundations, heap, observations and summaries suites. The proof_cache module doc and lib/README.md say which constructors are roots.

### application-core reuse R2: a read-only helper's footprint proved from its bytecode, lifted over it, and summarized from a proof of its own

change `wqlynuotqzut` · [log `6b3ea33ae1ea`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/6b3ea33ae1ea03437007ee782d57a6cf2bb49a89801356c6a39d57bc074a1be7.jsonl.gz)

R2's first part, in lib/src/reuse/footprint.rs (a submodule of reuse.rs, so no shared file changed), reuse::summarize and proof_cache::lifted_proof. footprint::footprint establishes a heap helper's read footprint from its bytecode rather than listing likely reads. The helper is an instance method no application class overrides, with primitive parameters and result. The only reference it handles is its receiver, loaded only to read a primitive field at once, and its static callees are walked under the same rules with no reference at all. So its getfields are all it reads of the heap, and since it writes nothing its outcome is a function of those fields' values and its arguments. The brief's exclusions (a write, an allocation, an exception of its own, a static field, an external call, a call on an object, an override, recursion, an escaping reference, an array) are each refused by name, and so are a division by anything but a non-zero constant, a switch and floating point.

footprint::lift is the explicit representation adapter: the helper as a static method of its own class over its arguments and then the values of the fields either version reads, with each field read replaced by a parameter. reuse::summarize proves the two versions' lifted helpers equal by a regression check of their own, under the caller's cache, engine and bounds and in the proof stack that keeps dependency proofs acyclic. It gives a spec::plans::Summary naming the proof's claim key, the fields and arguments read, the domain (every value of them, whatever else a receiver holds), and the proofs it rests on. A helper whose versions differ, or whose versions read fields the other's receiver doesn't declare alike, has none. No caller applies a summary yet; that, with the caller's claim carrying the summaries it used, is the next part.

Verified inline with a new tests/reuse_summaries.rs (5 tests): the frozen quote fixture's fee reads feeCents before and after, and its helper-extra-field defect also reads floorCents; 17 helpers outside the category are each refused in the words of their case; the lifting agrees with the helper on a real JVM over 560 cases, lifted over one field more than it reads; fee's summary has its proof verified in the cache, and an exact rerun gives the same summary with nothing new stored; the extra read and a layout change get no summary. The 231 unit tests, tests/reuse.rs (11), application_core (14), summaries, compare, heap, effects and foundations pass. Found: the lifted proof is positional in the fields' values, so a caller's claim must carry the whole summary (its reads), not only the proof's key; this is recorded under Progress for the next part. The contract's R2 row still stops at the objects stream's receiver refusal, as it checks fee through the plain regression entry point.

### application-core reuse R2: a changed caller reuses a read-only helper's summary at each call, through adapters that read the receiver there

change `stxzsnsyrspo` · [log `bdcda79bb98f`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/aa238023-596d-49bd-8039-52502ec096fc/bdcda79bb98f44a0d3978beb5acd9846cb0ba957c96d0e92783d9c020950f983.jsonl.gz)

Under --cache and the own checker, shared::plan_with now asks for a summary of each changed instance method both versions of a regression target call, declared by the same class. proof_cache::Helpers sends such a method to reuse::application, which makes the summary (its lifted proof from the cache, or proved now) and two call-site adapters (reuse::footprint::adapters). shared::substitute then rewrites every call of the helper, in both versions, into a static call of that version's adapter. The adapter reads each footprint field from the actual receiver as its own version lays it out, and calls the new version's lifted helper, so both versions call one function of the same values. Because the summary's proof covers every value of the fields and arguments, reading them at the call discharges applicability on the actual pre-call state: a receiver mutated between two calls is read twice, and a write through an aliasing parameter is seen. The caller's claim carries the whole summary as an assumption of kind summary, basis proved, with its proof's key (J3's helper assumptions). A helper with no summary keeps its body in both versions, with a note saying why.

Verified inline in lib/tests/reuse_summaries.rs (5 new tests, 10 in all, three runs). A tariff's rewritten fee is proved on its own, then reused by three changed callers, which are verified: one call, two calls around a mutation, and a write through another parameter with and without may_alias. A stale read after a mutation, and a read before an aliased write, are refuted with the summary applied, and their witnesses replay. A helper that reads an extra field, and helper versions that agree only on constructor-made receivers, get no summary. Their callers keep the body: the first is refuted, the second verified for a single call in the constructor domain and refuted, replayed, once a second call follows a lowered fee. On a JVM with -Xverify:all, the classes with the summary applied agree with the versions as written over a grid. Also passing: the 231 unit tests, reuse (11), application_core (14), summaries (40), compare, heap (49), effects (18), foundations (5) and observations (12). The contract's R2 row still stops at the objects stream's construction::receiver, since the quote's target is an instance method. That is for the merge.

**How it works**
- This only runs under `--cache` and the native engine. For each changed instance method that both versions call, the checker asks for that helper's summary, which comes from the proof cache or is proved on the spot.
- In both versions, every call of the helper is redirected to a small adapter for that version. The adapter reads the fields the helper uses from the actual object at that call, then calls the new version's version of the helper rewritten to take those field values as arguments.
- Because the helper's proof covers every value of those fields, reading them at each call is enough to make the summary apply there. A mutation between two calls is read twice, and a write through an aliasing parameter is seen.
- The caller's claim carries the whole summary, with its proof's key, so the helper assumptions now change the claim key as J3 requires.
- A helper with no summary keeps its own code in both versions, with a note saying why.

**Verified inline** in `lib/tests/reuse_summaries.rs`: 5 new tests, 10 in all, passing on three runs. The fixture is a `Tariff` class whose `fee` is rewritten and a changed caller class `Bill`.

**What job `20261108-060410` measured (release, on the joint example's builds):**
- An unchanged `compare` rerun took 290 ms as a process (210 ms in process). Of that, 185 ms went before the proofs even looked up the cache.

**What changed:**
- `lib/src/jimage.rs` now builds the image's table of classes once per process and shares it with every later open.
- The cache is keyed by the image's index bytes, which every open still reads, rather than by its path or a timestamp. A JDK changed in place therefore gets a fresh table.
- No proof cache key changed, and nothing is stored between runs.

**Verification:**
- A new unit test, which couldn't pass before the change, shows that two opens share one table, and that a copy of the index with one byte changed gets its own table.
- In a single debug run of the benchmark, an unchanged rerun dropped from 846 ms to 37 ms in process, with the same verdicts.
- The 234 unit tests and every suite I ran before pass.

# Application-core reuse loop: summary of this run (2 cycles)

The run made two commits on the reuse stream, in workspace `in-the-loop-application-core-reuse`. R2 is finished. R3's change is committed, but the job that measures it in a release build hasn't run yet.

## Commits

### 1. `xrxnwkqtkxuk`: R2, a read-only helper's summary now covers primitive arrays in its receiver's fields
**What it adds**
- A read-only helper (one that only reads its receiver's fields) can now also read an array held in one of those fields: its length and its elements. This works for one-dimensional primitive arrays, except float and double. The footprint analysis is in `lib/src/reuse/footprint.rs`.
- It checks every path through the helper's bytecode. Any array reference must stay in a local and only be used to get its length or load an element of its own type.
- These are each refused, by name:
  - writing to the array;
  - passing it on to another method;
  - comparing it or testing it for null;
  - two arrays meeting where paths join;
  - arrays of floats, of references, or of arrays.
- The summary's proof assumes the array isn't null and has at most 8 elements. Each version's adapter checks both facts on the real receiver at every call. If either fails, it runs that version's original helper instead.
- Each adapter is now a class of its own in its version's package, so it can legally reach package-private members.
